summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs focused on debugging flows for Atlas Health's production inference. Covered tracing UI, request log retention, export options, structured attributes for PII filtering, and how to map traces to request payloads for root-cause. Discussed hosted vs dedicated implications for logs and data residency; Diane asked about SOC2/KMS and on-prem options.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-21
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Atlas Head of Platform), Marco Chen (Atlas ML Eng), Diane Wu (Atlas Security)

[00:00] Ethan Park (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'm Ethan, account lead, with Priya who will run the tech walkthrough.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz (Atlas): Hi all, Lena here. We're mainly interested in debugging flows and log retention for PHI-safe prompts.
[00:18] Marco Chen (Atlas): Marco, will look at performance and tracing to map latency spikes.
[00:22] Diane Wu (Atlas): Diane, security lead — questions on encryption, KMS, and audit logs.
[00:28] Priya Singh (Redwood): Great, we'll demo the console tracing + request logs, show some error analysis, and highlight export options and filters. We'll also demo how traces map back to request payloads.

[02:05] Priya Singh (Redwood): Ok, starting screen share — this is the Redwood Console, Tracing tab. At a glance you can see aggregated latency distribution, error rate over time, and per-model breakdown. Note that the sampling is continuous but adjustable, we default to 5% for hosted; for dedicated you can set deterministic sampling.
[03:20] Marco Chen (Atlas): Small audio glitch there, but I see the charts. How granular are the traces? Can we get per-token timing?
[03:34] Priya Singh (Redwood): Good question — we capture stage-level timings: request receive, token generation, model inference, kv-cache restore, kernel execution. Per-token is available in dedicated deployments with high-overhead tracing enabled. For hosted, we give per-chunk timings which are usually enough to isolate slow model kernels.
[05:00] Lena Ortiz (Atlas): For compliance we need to avoid storing raw prompts with PHI, can we redact at ingestion?
[05:14] Priya Singh (Redwood): Yes, there are configurable redaction hooks — you can enable structured attributes and store only metadata+hashes. We also support on-the-fly PII detection to mask tokens before retention. Note that masking affects ability to replay exact requests.

[07:20] Ethan Park (Redwood): Marco, maybe show an example request that failed last week?
[07:28] Marco Chen (Atlas): Sure, here's an example where latency spiked to 3.2s and we saw token timeouts.
[07:40] Priya Singh (Redwood): Navigating to the Request Logs view — you can search by request id, model, route, or custom attribute. Here's the request id, and the trace pane shows a waterfall. You can expand stages and see error codes, kernel timings, and memory footprints.
[09:02] Marco Chen (Atlas): I see a big KV cache restore time. Is that because of a cold cache?
[09:16] Priya Singh (Redwood): Likely — KV cache misses on long context can add overhead. We automatically profile sequence length distribution and recommend batching/kv-prefetch settings in Optimize. We'll attach a recommended config after this call.

[11:05] Diane Wu (Atlas): On retention — what are default retention windows for request logs and traces in hosted? And can we export to S3?
[11:18] Priya Singh (Redwood): Hosted defaults to 30 days for full traces, 90 days for aggregated metrics. You can configure longer retention for paid tiers or export to customer S3 (redwood supports signed ingest to your bucket) or push logs to Splunk/Datadog via connectors. For Private deployment you control retention entirely.
[13:40] Lena Ortiz (Atlas): If we export to S3, is that encrypted with our KMS?
[13:50] Priya Singh (Redwood): Yes — for exports we support SSE-KMS and you can provide your key for the bucket. For Private we can also integrate with your HSM but that requires an enterprise add-on.

[16:02] Priya Singh (Redwood): Switching to Error Analysis — this is the workbench where you can group errors, create a cluster of NLU failures, hallucinations, or model timeouts. You can attach example prompts and ground-truth responses to build a regression test set.
[17:45] Marco Chen (Atlas): Can we link a failing request back to a user id without leaking PHI?
[17:58] Priya Singh (Redwood): Yes, we recommend storing a hashed user id or a nonce as a custom attribute. The console supports lookup tables to map nonce to internal ids in your secure vault if you need one-off debugging.

[20:10] Priya Singh (Redwood): I'm going to run a live search. Typing the request id into the search bar — here is the raw event row. Notice the quick-links: Replay (sandboxed), Export payload (redacted), Open trace. Replay runs in a sandbox that strips PII unless you have opted into deep replay for dedicated/private clusters.
[21:45] Marco Chen (Atlas): That replay feature would be huge for our SREs. How deterministic is replay versus the original run?
[21:57] Priya Singh (Redwood): Replays are best-effort — for stochastic models you can set a seed, same temperature and model version will often reproduce the same tokens but not guaranteed unless you pin the model commit and use same KV cache state. We surface those caveats in the UI.

[24:05] Diane Wu (Atlas): Audit logs — can we get immutable logs of who viewed traces or exported data?
[24:18] Ethan Park (Redwood): Yes, we have audit logs that show user actions, IP, timestamp, and object touched. For hosted customers on enterprise tiers we can forward audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud connectors.
[25:40] Marco Chen (Atlas): On performance — do you have recommended thresholds to trigger autoscaling? We saw bursty traffic; we'd like graceful degradation rather than errors.
[25:55] Priya Singh (Redwood): For Dedicated you can set CPU/GPU queue depth based policies and model-level fallback. There's an automatic fallback to a quantized variant if latency SLOs are breached. In the console you can set SLO alerts and a routing policy.

[28:10] Priya Singh (Redwood): Now a short demo of correlating traces to resource metrics — you can overlay GPU util, memory usage, and kernel-level counters onto the trace waterfall. This helps identify whether a slowdown was I/O, kernel, or model related.
[29:40] Marco Chen (Atlas): I'm seeing kernel stalls aligned with GPU memory spikes — is there a way to pre-warm KV cache?
[29:52] Priya Singh (Redwood): Yes, Optimize suggests prefetch windows and batching; you can also use a warmup API that pre-populates cache entries. We'll include recommended warmup script in follow-up.

[32:05] Diane Wu (Atlas): Network egress — logs show IP addresses for servicing nodes; can we restrict via VPC peering or Private deployment?
[32:20] Priya Singh (Redwood): For Private and Dedicated, you can peer into your VPC or choose no-egress mode. Hosted does have egress but we support static IP ranges and allowlisting.

[34:10] Ethan Park (Redwood): Quick note on integrations — we can push traces to Datadog or export to BigQuery for long-term analytics. Also have a CSV/JSON bulk export for compliance teams.
[34:46] Lena Ortiz (Atlas): For our legal/compliance review we'll need the SOC2 report and details on encryption in transit at rest.
[34:56] Ethan Park (Redwood): We'll send SOC2 and the network diagram. Diane, Priya will follow up on the KMS/HSM options.

[36:30] Priya Singh (Redwood): Wrapping up with a short troubleshooting flow — find a request by id, open trace, inspect waterfall, check kernel timings, check kv-cache hit/miss, then check request attributes for user context. If needed, replay in sandbox or export payload (redacted) to reproduce in dedicated env.
[38:05] Marco Chen (Atlas): Sounds good. Could you run a short benchmark on our sample prompts?
[38:16] Priya Singh (Redwood): Yes — we'll run a 1000-request batch with your prompts and share the results and recommended config.

[40:00] Ethan Park (Redwood): Recap of next steps: we'll share recording and pricing deck, Priya will run the benchmark and send the CSV by next week, and we'll provide SOC2 + KMS docs. Any other questions?
[40:20] Diane Wu (Atlas): One more — what's the lead time for Private deployment?
[40:30] Priya Singh (Redwood): Typically 8-12 weeks depending on network approvals and hardware procurement; we can fast-track in some cases.
[41:05] Lena Ortiz (Atlas): OK great, thanks everyone.
[41:12] Ethan Park (Redwood): Thanks all, we'll follow up via email.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present — names like "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "kay vee cache"; small filler words removed for clarity. Links shared during call: https://redwood.ai/console-demo (demo recording), https://redwood.ai/soc2-summary (SOC2), and a shared spreadsheet link referenced as "Benchmark - Atlas" (internal link).
questions: Can Redwood redact PHI at ingestion without losing debugging capability?
How deterministic are replays for stochastic models?
What is the export path for audit logs to SIEM?
